data.name: Maran
data.gender_notes: Maran is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Maran represents the god of death. He is the one who ends all life and takes the soul to the next world. Maran is a powerful and feared deity, symbolizing the inevitability of death and the cycle of life and rebirth. The name Maran carries the meaning “Death” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Maran usually hope their child will grow to embody death and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Maran belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Death.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maran total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Maran holds great significance in Hindu culture as it represents the god of death. It is a reminder of the cyclical nature of life and the inevitability of death. Maran is depicted in various art forms, mythological stories, and religious rituals.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Maran represents the end of one life cycle and the beginning of another. He is a reminder of the impermanence of life and the importance of living in the present moment. Maran is also a symbol of detachment and letting go, as the soul leaves the physical body and transcends into the next world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Maran is a Sanskrit word meaning 'death'. It is believed that acknowledging and embracing the concept of death helps one lead a more mindful and purposeful life. Maran is also a name of Lord Yama, the Hindu god of death.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Maran was a general in the army of King Krishna during the Mahabharata war. The name Maran carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Maran was a loyal and brave warrior who fought on the side of the Pandava army against the Kauravas.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Maran continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
